To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a-tDCS has differential long-lasting effects on MEPs elicited in suprahyoid muscles depending on the side of the brain where the stimulation is applied.
tDCS has long-lasting effects on MEPs elicited on the stimulated hemisphere, while the effects on the non-stimulated hemisphere depend on the site of application of tDCS.
anodal tCDS (a-tDC) has differential effects on bilateral suprahyoid MEP when applied over either the hemisphere with stronger or the hemisphere with weaker projections, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new therapeutic approach for patients with swallowing disorders.
the effects of anodical transcranial direct current stimulations (tDCSs) on the human swallowing system.
the development of non-invasive brain stimulation methods to modulate cortical motor plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a-tDCS modulates MEPs from the targeted hemisphere, and additionally, when the stimulation is performed over the hemisphere with weaker projections, MEPs can also be modulated in the non-targeted contralateral hemisphere.
the bilateral effects of tDCS are not only dependent on the stimulation site, but also on the strength of the projection of the stimulated area.
a-tDCS can induce long-lasting changes in motor cortex excitability and that these effects can be modulated by concurrent task execution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a-tDCS has differential long-lasting effects on bilateral suprahyoid MEP depending on the site stimulation.
anodal t-DCS has a differential impact on the bilateral suprahyoid motor system depending on the hemisphere that is targeted for stimulation.
the application of a tDCS over the hemisphere with weaker projections leads to bilateral plasticity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of tDCS are not restricted to the stimulated hemisphere but also affect the contralateral hemisphere, which may be important for clinical applications.
the application of a single tDCS session over one hemisphere may lead to a bilateral effect.
the effects of anode-tDCS on the suprahyoid motor system are not limited to the targeted hemisphere.
